resources.string: Warns about calls from mass-traffic (0137), service (0180) and premium (0900) numbers, which cost extra to call back.
Warns about calls from numbers starting 400, which Spanish law reserves for commercial calls from 17 October 2026.
Warns about calls from the numbers ARCEP reserved for automated calling platforms (Numéros Polyvalents Vérifiés): 01 62, 01 63, 02 70, 02 71, 03 77, 03 78, 04 24, 04 25, 05 68, 05 69, 09 48, 09 49.
From 22:00 to 07:00 only your contacts ring and everyone else is silenced. Repeat callers still get through.
Calls from any country other than your SIM\'s are silenced (they still appear in Recents). Contacts, allowed numbers and repeat callers still ring.
Numbers that can\'t exist or aren\'t assigned in their country (a common sign of spoofing) are silenced.
Warns about calls from the 140 series, which TRAI requires for promotional (telemarketing) voice calls. The 1600 series used for banking and government service calls is never touched.
Warns about calls from 0844 (market research, advertising and sales) and 0843 (statistical surveys), the codes AGCOM reserved for call centres.
UK: premium, service and 070 personal numbers
Warns about calls from 070 personal numbers, 0843/0844/0845 and 087 service numbers, and 09 premium-rate numbers. Calling them back can be expensive.
Gives a low-score warning for calls that show a toll-free number (800, 833, 844, 855, 866, 877, 888). Robocallers often spoof these, and real businesses rarely call from them.
